verdict.rationale: React is a library, so its public API is its documented JavaScript interface. The react.dev reference documents entry points such as createRoot and hydrateRoot, including options like onUncaughtError and identifierPrefix, and the llms.txt probe shows the docs are published in an agent-consumable form. No HTTP/OpenAPI surface exists (the probe returned 404), which fits a client-side library rather than signalling a gap. Missing for 10: evidence of breadth across the full API reference (hooks, server APIs) beyond a few entry points, and independent or hands-on corroboration of agents driving React through this API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: createRoot lets you create a root to display React components inside a browser DOM node.
hydrateRoot lets you display React components inside a browser DOM node whose HTML content was previously generated by react-dom/server.
onUncaughtError: Callback called when an error is thrown and not caught by an Error Boundary.
identifierPrefix: A string prefix React uses for IDs generated by useId.
